media-reviews/boys-club.html.title: boys club
media-reviews/boys-club.html.description: hello everybody this is jojo and right now im reviewing the comic boys club. the small series of comics follow 4 slacker/stoner roommates: andy, landwolf, brett and the most known out of the bunch pepe the frog. throughout the comic they get into a bunch of comedic mischief similar to college frat boys and stoner humor like cheech and chong. its an ok comic with a few comedic moments that people the age 25 or under would enjoy. overall, this comic is a good read if you are into that sort of stuff.

media-reviews/sensory-life-on-the-spectr.title: sensory life on the spectrum
media-reviews/sensory-life-on-the-spectr.description: hello everybody this is jojo and today im going to review sensory: life on the spectrum. Sensory: Life on the Spectrum" is a vibrant and heartfelt anthology that offers a unique glimpse into the lives of autistic individuals through the medium of comics. this collection features contributions from thirty autistic creators, each sharing their personal experiences, challenges, and triumphs. The comics cover a wide range of topics, from the journey to diagnosis to finding community and coping mechanisms for sensory overload. The illustrations are as diverse as the stories themselves, ranging from soft, paint-like depictions to jagged, dark drawings, each adding a distinct emotional depth to the narratives. Overall, "Sensory: Life on the Spectrum" is a must-read for anyone looking to explore the autistic experience through a creative and engaging format. It's a testament to the strength and resilience of autistic individuals and a celebration of their diverse voices.

media-reviews/the-pervert.html.title: the pervert
media-reviews/the-pervert.html.description: The Pervert is a raw and unflinching exploration of identity, sexuality, and survival. Written by Remy Boydell and Michelle Perez, this graphic novel stands out for its brave storytelling and unique artwork. The narrative follows a transgender sex worker navigating life in Seattle, and it doesn't shy away from the harsh realities and complex emotions associated with this journey.The writing is brutally honest, offering a candid look at the protagonist's experiences, struggles, and moments of resilience. Perez's dialogue is sharp and impactful, effectively conveying the internal and external conflicts faced by the main character.Boydell's art style complements the narrative beautifully, with watercolor illustrations that are both delicate and powerful. The use of color and composition adds depth to the story, enhancing the emotional weight of each scene.What sets The Pervert apart is its commitment to authenticity. shrines/dragonball-z.html.title: dragonball z
shrines/dragonball-z.html.description: as for many people my age dragonball z was my first introduction to the world of anime. i used to watch it on toonami with my cousin and brother after school everyday when it came on cartoon network. I enjoyed watching goku and all the other z fighters go on adventures and fight enemys and the bad guys. I remember this anime series very fondly. till this very day im still a fan of dragonball z and anime as a whole.

shrines/pokemon.html.title: pokemon
shrines/pokemon.html.description: for those that dont know pokemon is a game, anime series and card game that started in the 90s. I have fond memories of pokemon because i used to watch it on tv everyday after school with my brother and cousin. i remember having fun watching ash and his friends go on adventures and being excited where the story will go next. also, i had a green gameboy color that i played the living crap of pokemon yellow on. it was a good time and pokemon gives me good memories till this very day. I still enjoy playing the pokemon games they hold up very well in my eyes.

shrines/toonami.html.title: toonami
shrines/toonami.html.description: when i was little i would watch toonami after school everyday and watch anime. For those that dont know toonami was a tv programming block that played anime on cartoon network. like many people my age that is how i got into anime. from dragonball to naruto i watched all sorts of anime on toonami when i was little. i wouldn't been introduced to great shows if it wasn't for toonami. till this day i still like anime and cartoons. so yeah, thanks toonami for the memories.

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
